summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, laryngeal stenosis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for evaluation of worsening dysphagia and odynophagia. She reported a three-day history of sore throat and difficulty swallowing, with coughing after liquids. Initial workup showed normal labs and a clear chest X-ray. Speech and swallow evaluation revealed improved swallowing with tracheostomy occlusion, and an EGD showed no mechanical obstruction. Her symptoms were attributed to pharyngeal residue, and she was successfully managed with behavioral strategies. She tolerated a regular diet with technique modification, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up instructions.
